entities.summary: The Delta IV Heavy was an expendable heavy-lift launch vehicle, the largest member of the Delta IV family. Following the retirement of the Space Shuttle in 2011, it was the most capable operational launch vehicle until the Falcon Heavy's debut in 2018. At the time of its retirement in 2024, it ranked third among active rockets in payload capacity. Developed by Boeing and later manufactured by United Launch Alliance (ULA), it first flew in 2004. The Delta IV Heavy was retired after its 16th and final launch on 9 April 2024 and was succeeded by ULA's Vulcan Centaur rocket, which can offer similar heavy-lift capabilities at a lower cost with a single-core and six solid rocket boosters.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Delta IV Heavy played a significant role in the launch of critical satellites and spacecraft for NASA's Deep Space Network, including the Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity Rover) and the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter. Its retirement marked the end of an era in heavy-lift launch capabilities.
